claims.statement: playRandomQueue filters playable songs, applies mood-slot candidate filtering when active, delegates to RandomQueuePlanner.planRandomQueue, and on success exits infinite mode, replaces the in-memory recent-played set with the plan's, and starts the batch via setPlayQueue(plan.songs, 0, PlayMode.SEQUENTIAL); it returns false and starts nothing when no songs are playable.

RandomQueuePlanner batches by neededSize = minOf(DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE=20, playable pool size), excludes recentSongIds from selection, and when the remainder falls below the batch it clears the recent set (resetHistory=true) and reuses the whole pool; trimToLimit caps the returned recent set to the playable library size, dropping earliest-inserted ids first. With uniform random off the selection is shuffle(pool).take(batch) shuffled again.

UniformRandomPlanner.selectSongs groups candidates by raw play count (playCounts[id] ?: 0) into ascending tiers — tier 0 = smallest-count group, tier 1 = next, remaining groups flattened as fallback — and fills the quota by tier priority with in-tier shuffling, never crossing into higher tiers while a lower tier has songs. Thresholds derive from the current distribution, so tiering survives when every song has been played past any fixed threshold, and equal counts degenerate to a single tier (pure shuffle). With the flag off it plain-shuffles.

UniformRandomPlanner.orderSongs and buildPlayOrderIds provide count-tiered play-mode ordering (current song first for SHUFFLE), but production wiring installs QueueManager.defaultPlayOrderBuilder in app/di/PlayerModule, so the SHUFFLE play mode stays pure shuffle and independent of uniform random; the tiered builders are the prepared bodies should the PlayOrderBuilder seam ever become settings-aware.

The uniform-random switch is carried on PlayerUiState.globalUniformRandomEnabled (default true), persisted by PlayerSettingsRepository (DataStore with legacy-SharedPreferences fallback true), loaded into UI state at PlayerRuntime.start(), and toggled from Settings via setGlobalUniformRandomEnabled. Changing the setting only writes the flag — it never reshuffles the live queue or its playOrderIds; it takes effect on the next random selection, infinite refill batch, or future queue rebuild.

PlayerRandomQueueFacade receives play counts through an injected rawPlayCounts callable (default empty); PlayerRuntime wires it to PlayStatsRepository.getRawPlayCounts (Room-backed raw play count, distinct from the effective count used for sorting), and playRandomQueue queries it per candidate pool at call time for both lucky and explore batches.

startInfinitePlay keeps the current queue untouched: planInfiniteStart only records the queued playable song ids as the infinitePlayedSongIds coverage set, and an empty queue is legal (mode starts armed, waiting for refills). If the controller is already near the tail (remainingMediaItems() <= 5) it refills immediately, so the next track (natural end or system media keys) is a new song instead of a REPEAT_MODE_ALL wrap back to the old window's first item. startInfinitePlay refuses to start while an explore session is active (isExplorePlay).

Infinite-queue refills are triggered by PlayerMediaEventFacade.handleMediaItemEnded (fires on every user navigation track transition; refills when wrapped or remaining <= DEFAULT_REFILL_THRESHOLD=5, passing advanceAfterWrap=wrapped) and by PlayerPlaybackFacade.playNext when planNext returns RefillInfiniteQueue; a pending skipNextRefill (set by add-to-next) is consumed instead of refilling so an inserted next song is not pushed back. In explore mode the same handleMediaItemEnded additionally settles the ended song and triggers the explore refill.

planInfiniteRefill sizes the batch like lucky play, excludes both the coverage set (playedSongIds) and songs already in the queue, clears the coverage set with resetHistory=true when the unplayed remainder is below the batch, and always selects through UniformRandomPlanner (the flag decides tiered vs plain shuffle); empty selection leaves the queue untouched, otherwise songs are appended via PlayQueue.withSongs which preserves the current item's index.

PlaybackController detects a window-tail wrap by index (isMediaItemWrap: new index 0 and previous index >= mediaItemCount-1, and previous index > new index) rather than by transition reason, because Media3 reports a REPEAT_MODE_ALL tail wrap as SEEK (manual) or AUTO (natural end) while MEDIA_ITEM_TRANSITION_REASON_REPEAT only means single-item repeat; AUTO/SEEK/REPEAT transitions all route to onMediaItemEnded, so headset/lock-screen/notification skips also refill infinite mode.

On refill after a wrap (advanceAfterWrap=true), the facade sets the business queue's current index to the pre-append queue length — the first newly appended song — and starts it through playFromQueue (error-checked queue start) instead of syncPlayerQueue, so the user hears new songs rather than the replayed old window; when no new songs were added it keeps the current song and neither plays nor syncs.

Mood time-slot filtering happens at the planner entry, not inside the planners: when the slot is active, filterByMoodTags narrows the candidate pool to songs whose emotion tags intersect the slot's tags AT OR ABOVE MoodSlotPolicy.MATCH_MIN_RATIO (0.35), so a tag the model isn't confident about no longer qualifies the song; tiered selection plus recent eviction are reused unchanged on that pool (uniform random composes). An empty filtered pool logs 'fall back to full library' and returns null so playback falls back to full-library random, and pools below MoodSlotPolicy.POOL_WARN_THRESHOLD=10 log a loop warning. The ratio match uses the injected moodEmotionTagRatiosOf (user-manual tags match at 1.0; the default derives 1.0 per tag so nothing changes without injection). Slot configs and emotion-tag ratio maps are Volatile snapshots on PlayerRuntime fed by a continuous Room/DataStore stream subscription (match vs vote distributions computed separately), with an injectable nowMinuteOfDay. Mood filtering is bypassed when explore mode is active.

The lucky-play and infinite-play entry wiring lives in the app shell, not AppNavHost: NowPlayingSurface wires onLuckyPlayClick → playerViewModel.playRandomQueue { started, moodSlotName -> ... } and onStartInfinitePlay → playerViewModel.startInfinitePlay { started, moodSlotName -> ... }; AppRoot duplicates the lucky-play wiring for the empty-queue LuckyPlayEntryBar. HomeRouteActions (feature/home) exposes the onLuckyPlayClick / onStartInfinitePlay / onStopInfinitePlay callback trio (typed () -> Unit) whose implementations live in the app shell, and HomeRoute itself routes the infinite button to a hint dialog while an explore session is active. The facades are async with a result callback (raw-play-count querying runs off the main thread), and on success the caller shows the mood attribution toast '已按「$slotName」为你随机播放' (lucky) or '已按「$slotName」开启无限随机播放' (infinite), with failure showing the import hint '还没有可播放的音乐，请先导入歌曲吧~'; both actions also reset the playlist-resume source via playlistResumeViewModel.switchSource(null, ...). The attribution delegates to the same activeMoodSlot() evaluation the random decision used, so the attribution can never disagree with the applied filter.

Lucky-play eviction history (recentPlayedSongIds) is in-memory only and resets with the process, while isInfinitePlay and infinitePlayedSongIds are persisted through PlaybackStateStore (IS_INFINITE_PLAY / INFINITE_PLAYED_IDS alongside the queue JSON) and restored with saved played-ids filtered to songs still in the library (an empty queue may restore while infinite mode is on via allowEmpty=isInfinitePlay), so infinite play survives process death. The same save/restore also persists isExplorePlay under IS_EXPLORE_PLAY, so a mid-explore session resumes. PlayerPersistenceFacade.savePlaybackStateAsync captures the position and full state snapshot on the caller thread and only then moves the DataStore write to IO via an injected suspending launchIo, threading the up-front position so an IO save cannot read a stale position; PlaybackStateStore.save also skips writing an empty-session queue that would clobber an existing snapshot. Infinite mode exits via stopInfinitePlay, via setPlayQueue's default exitInfinitePlay=true, or explicitly in playRandomQueue; playRelatedSongs is the exception that keeps it on, re-seeding infinitePlayedSongIds with the new current+related queue so refills reach outside it.

The random chain is locked by tests that must stay green before changing it: RandomQueuePlannerTest (eviction, resetHistory, uniform selection after filtering, infinite start/refill exclusions, explore refill), UniformRandomPlannerTest (tier preemption, dynamic tiering beyond fixed thresholds, equal-count degeneration, orderSongs grouping), PlayerRandomQueueFacadeTest (start/refill/wrap semantics, the mood-filter scenarios including uniform compatibility, and the explore generation/session/refill-tiering cases), PlayerMediaEventFacadeTest (tail and wrap refill triggers plus the explore settle/refill triggers), and MediaItemWrapDetectionTest (index-based wrap rule edge cases).

Explore playback is gated by RandomEnhanceMode (OFF / TIME_SLOT / EXPLORE), where TIME_SLOT (mood-slot filtering) and EXPLORE are mutually exclusive enhancement modes layered on the same RandomQueuePlanner core. PlayerRuntime reads playerSettingsRepository.randomEnhanceMode as a stream, driving moodSlotEnabled (TIME_SLOT) and exploreModeEnabled / isExploreModeActive (EXPLORE), so mode toggles are reflected live. Both gates read a cached @Volatile randomEnhanceModeCache kept fresh by the same stream observer (zero DataStore reads per call) rather than calling .first() each time.

In explore mode, playRandomQueue bypasses mood-slot filtering entirely (mood = if (explore) null else activeMoodSlot()), plans a fixed 10-song batch (ExplorePlaybackPolicy.INITIAL_BATCH_SIZE via planner.batchSize override, default stays 20 otherwise), still applies recent-skip eviction and the uniform-random flag within that batch, and on success writes isExplorePlay = explore to PlayerUiState while exiting infinite mode.

ExplorePlaybackPolicy (pure, JVM-testable, no Android deps) fixes the explore constants: INITIAL_BATCH_SIZE=10, REFILL_COUNT=5, REFILL_THRESHOLD=0, MIN_LISTEN_MS=30_000, MIN_LISTEN_RATIO=0.25, VOTE_MIN_RATIO=EmotionGroup.MIN_RATIO (0.15, same threshold as detail-page display), VOTE_MAX_TAGS=EmotionGroup.MAX_TAGS (4), and VOTE_WEIGHT_SCALE=100 (integer ratio votes; a one-time history ×100 migration kept scale). voteWeightOf(ratio)=round(ratio×100) and votesOf maps ratios to integer weights dropping zero; isSkipped(playedMs, durationMs) returns true (a dislike-worthy quick skip) when the listener heard <30s OR <1/4 of the total duration; with an unknown duration (<=0) it applies only the 30-second rule.

WordPreference is a vote-accumulating model (not a boolean toggle): each emotion word independently accumulates likeVotes/dislikeVotes and kind (LIKE/DISLIKE/NEUTRAL) is the vote-majority winner (tie = NEUTRAL). likeSharePercent reports the liked share of votes rather than raw tallies because vote weights are ratios×100. Because a word can never be on both sides and a single skip never immediately flips a previously-liked word, it resolves 'same song already liked A/B and disliked C/D' cross-song conflicts.

Explore word learning is triggered in handleMediaItemEnded: it captures the just-ended song's id and actual listen ms (trackedSongId()/currentPlayedMs()) before stopPlaybackTracking() clears them; only when both isExplorePlay and isExploreModeActive are set does it call onExploreSongSettled(songId, playedMs). PlayerRuntime.handleExploreSongSettled applies isSkipped and, using the song's vote distribution (separate from the match distribution), keeps only words at or above VOTE_MIN_RATIO (top VOTE_MAX_TAGS, the tags the detail page shows), converts each ratio to an integer vote weight via ExplorePlaybackPolicy.votesOf (dropping zero weights), and calls wordPreferenceRepository.recordSongOutcome(votes, liked = !skipped) — a full listen casts ratio-weighted like votes on the displayed tags; a fast skip casts dislike votes on the same tags.

Explore queue refill is triggered by the same handleMediaItemEnded after computing remainingSongs = remainingMediaItems(); when the ended song was second-to-last (remaining <= REFILL_THRESHOLD=0, measured after the track change), it calls refillExplorePlayQueue(startedSongId). 1 remaining (third-to-last) does NOT refill, because the business queue's currentIndex is not yet synced to the controller and refilling that early could re-pull to the old song. The explore threshold is injected separately (exploreRefillThreshold) from the infinite threshold (DEFAULT_REFILL_THRESHOLD=5).

refillExplorePlayQueue is a no-op outside an explore session; it first corrects the business queue's current item to startedSongId via withCurrentSongId (otherwise the sync would yank playback back to the old song), builds a preference-tiered pool with buildExploreRefillPool, and appends exploration decisions through planner.planExploreRefill then syncPlayerQueue.

buildExploreRefillPool tiers the library by learned word preference in strict fallback order with a REFILL_COUNT-sufficiency gate (not mere non-emptiness, 2026-10-25 fix): (1) if neither liked nor disliked words exist yet, the full library; (2) songs carrying >=1 liked word AND no disliked word, if that pool holds >= REFILL_COUNT songs; (3) songs carrying no disliked word, if that pool holds >= REFILL_COUNT songs; (4) the full library. This guarantees refill always tops up to REFILL_COUNT whenever the library has enough songs outside the queue, preventing the all-DISLIKE self-lock. Word classification comes from wordPreferenceOf(word).kind.

planExploreRefill takes count songs randomly from a caller-prefiltered pool, excludes anything already in the queue, and appends via queue.withSongs (preserving the current index); an empty candidate pool yields an empty addedSongs and the queue is left untouched. Unlike planInfiniteRefill, it does not consult uniform random or play counts — it is a plain shuffle over the preference-tiered pool.

The explore session flag is isExplorePlay, which governs (not the settings mode): startInfinitePlay refuses to start while isExplorePlay is true ('blocked by explore session'). Manual queue replacement through PlayerQueueFacade.applyPlan clears isExplorePlay=false for any queue-replacing plan with exitInfinitePlay=true (a user picking a song exits the session, reverting the button to infinite random), so after exit startInfinitePlay succeeds even if the settings mode is still EXPLORE (asserted by exploreSessionEndedAllowsInfinitePlay).

When the randomEnhanceMode stream leaves EXPLORE while an explore session is running, PlayerRuntime calls randomQueueFacade.stopExplorePlay() (clearing isExplorePlay). A process restart mid-explore re-enters the session because isExplorePlay is persisted to PlaybackStateStore under IS_EXPLORE_PLAY, while the settings-derived isExploreModeActive re-arms from the randomEnhanceMode stream. Word preferences are persisted (Room-backed WordPreferenceRepository stream) and survive restarts to shape future buildExploreRefillPool runs.
